component.name: Wheelguard
component.summary: Scroll bounce filter and advanced settings for your mouse

description.p: Wheelguard drops the bouncing, wrong-direction scroll-wheel ticks of a faulty encoder on GNOME, with a live view of the wheel. It also edits the on-board settings of the Endgame Gear XM2w 4k v2 (DPI, polling rate, lift-off distance, button filtering, sleep timers and battery), the Logitech G Pro X Superlight (DPI stages, polling rate, battery) and the Razer DeathAdder V4 Pro (DPI stages, polling rate up to 8000 Hz, sleep timer, low-battery warning, battery), and the GNOME pointer settings. Not affiliated with Endgame Gear, Logitech or Razer.

screenshot.caption: Scroll protection with the live wheel monitor
The mouse's own settings: battery, DPI stages and more

ul.li: New: Scroll speed. A slider on the Scroll protection page sets how far one notch of the wheel scrolls, from 50% to 300%, for the mouse Wheelguard protects (GNOME has no setting for it)
Click-Lock works for left-handed use: with GNOME's left-handed switch on, it watches the right button of the mouse, which is then your main button
The Double-click fix now also covers the two thumb buttons (Back and Forward), and the Clicks page counts them
The background service does about 30% less work for every report of the mouse, so it uses less processor time while the mouse moves (most at 4000 and 8000 Hz polling)
Looking for the mouse no longer opens the computer's other input devices (keyboards, touchpads): Wheelguard reads what the kernel shows about them and opens only the mouse

A mouse that was asleep when Wheelguard started at login is picked up by itself: the panel's battery and DPI stages, the low-battery alerts and the profiles' DPI switch no longer wait for the popup or the Mouse page to be opened

Fifteen more Logitech G mice are recognised: G Pro Wireless, G Pro Hero, G305, G102 / G203, G303 Shroud Edition, G403 Hero, G502 Hero, G502 Lightspeed, G502 X, G502 X Lightspeed, G502 X Plus, G604, G703 Hero, G705 and G903 Hero
They are protected automatically, and the Mouse page and panel show their battery, DPI stages and polling rate; changing settings stays off until each model has been tested
Ten more Razer mice are recognised: DeathAdder V3 Pro and V3 HyperSpeed, Viper V2 Pro, V3 Pro, V3 Pro SE, V3 HyperSpeed and Mini Signature Edition, Basilisk V3 Pro and V3 Pro 35K, Cobra Pro
They are protected automatically, and the Mouse page and panel show their battery, DPI stages, polling rate and sleep timer; changing settings stays off until each model has been tested
Battery for any wireless mouse: the panel icon, tray and low-battery alerts now show the battery Linux reports for a mouse Wheelguard has no driver for (read-only, through UPower)
Automatic now protects the mice you allowed, so a mouse stays protected after Allow this mouse even when you switch between mice; a supported mouse still comes first
Remove access is offered for an allowed mouse that Automatic is protecting
Friendlier wording when Wheelguard finds a mouse it doesn't know yet
Allow this mouse: one button and your administrator password let Wheelguard protect a mouse it doesn't know, so scroll protection, Click-Lock and the Double-click fix work with any wheel mouse
Take the access back any time with Remove access
New Clicks page for Click-Lock and the Double-click fix, and a Settings page; choose the mouse to protect from the status pill at the top of the window
Pause: a shortcut (Super+Alt+P) or the Pause button makes Wheelguard let go of the mouse until you resume
Per-game profiles no longer change your saved settings, and work for games started from Lutris, Heroic or Wine
The Mouse page is split into sections, and follows the mouse being protected when two are connected
Click-Lock ends when the screen locks even with the app closed; "ignore drags" follows your DPI
The Double-click fix shows which button needed it
After an update the app offers to restart itself or the service
Fixed: a clock change could stretch or shorten the filter's timing
Fixed: on a high-resolution scroll wheel, a held partial step came out as a whole notch
Fixed: scroll protection didn't find the Logitech G Pro X Superlight behind its receiver and kept saying "Waiting for mouse"
When only a mouse Wheelguard doesn't support is connected, the app now says so instead of "can't see the mouse"
Fixed: when the computer was busy, a click could get lost, or the left button could stay pressed and swallow the next click
Per-game profiles: pick an app, such as a game, and Wheelguard switches scroll protection, Click-Lock and the DPI stage while it is in front, then back to your settings
Double-click fix: ignores the extra click a worn mouse button sends, for every mouse
Scroll protection works with any mouse that has a wheel; pick it in the new Mouse box
Wheel health: a 7 and 30 day chart of how often the wheel needed blocking, with a warning if it starts bouncing more
Click-Lock lets go by itself after 10 minutes (adjustable), and when the computer sleeps or the screen locks
Click-Lock in Repeat mode no longer starts while you are dragging
Low-battery alerts at 20% and 5%, with an amber dot on the panel icon
Keyboard shortcuts for Click-Lock and the next DPI stage, added from the About page
A drawing of your mouse on the Mouse page that lights up the button you are editing
A short welcome for new users that checks the mouse, permissions and protection strength
The status pill shows your mouse's real name and how it is connected
Calmer panel popup when the mouse is asleep; hover the icon to see the battery
Copy diagnostics: one click on About copies a privacy-safe report for bug reports
Works with screen readers and the keyboard, and follows GNOME's Large Text and Reduce Animation settings
The mouse is picked up the moment it wakes or is plugged in
The background service runs in a tight sandbox: read-only system and home folder, no network
Fixed: a click at the moment Wheelguard took over the mouse could leave the button stuck
Fixed: clicks and scrolls made while Wheelguard was starting could happen twice
Fixed: a broken config file or bad request could stop the scroll filter
Fixed: mouse settings could be saved only partly (Endgame sleep timer) or to an empty DPI stage (Logitech)
Fixed: the panel popup could show controls after the app had closed
Click-Lock: hold the left button and Wheelguard keeps clicking (or keeps it pressed) until your next click
Switch it, pick the mode and set the hold time from the panel popup or the Pointer page
New mice: Logitech G Pro X Superlight (first generation) and Razer DeathAdder V4 Pro
Fixed: the left button could stay pressed after the mouse woke up or reconnected
One package for every Fedora release, independent of the Python version
Signed packages from a DNF repository that keeps itself configured
The panel icon works on GNOME 51 (Fedora 45)
